quest.title: The Farmer's Treasure
quest.description: Saimon Jirou, a son of a farming family, dreams of finding treasure, but has met with an unexpected crisis instead...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Primogem x60, Saimon Heirloom Blade Diagram x1, Northlander Sword Billet x1

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
dialogues.text: Ho there, youngster! I do not recognize your face. Did you see the notice as well?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you talking to me?

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
dialogues.text: Yes, haha. Does it appear like anyone else nearby is young?

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
dialogues.text: Oh dear, where are my manners?

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
dialogues.text: Well met, youngster.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
dialogues.text: I believe you must have seen that notice earlier. As you may suspect, I am Saimon Katsumi.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
dialogues.text: It brings me no small amount of shame to ask outsiders to help me find that useless son of mine...

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
dialogues.text: But please, do tell me if you hear of anything regarding him, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
dialogues.text: No matter if that little brat is alive, or... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
dialogues.text: Please tell me everything you know truthfully.

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: You have my thanks. Truly...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's fine, leave it to us!

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: Ah yes, youngster. Let me also say that if you're able to enter and exit military camps... you could simply ask that lad's comrades-in-arms.

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: There's another young lad who joined the army together with him. Ishikawa, I think his name was. A military family's son, and a reliable one at that.

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: I'm sorry to have kept you here for so long. Still, if you receive any new, don't forget to swing by Konda Village and inform me.

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: Alright, I need to go back to the village now. Stay safe, youngster.

dialogues.speaker: Ono
dialogues.text: Hello there, outlander.

dialogues.speaker: Ono
dialogues.text: Are you one of those "advisors" sent by the Lord Commissioner to teach us how to fight our wars? If you are, you can just go look for Lord Masahito.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Saimon Katsumi asked us to come here.

dialogues.speaker: Ono
dialogues.text: Hmph. You outlanders have no manners. Mr. Saimon is well-respected around here. How could you address him without any honorifics?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're not that polite yourself!

response.speaker: Ono
response.text: ...Alright, I get it. This isn't the time to be arguing about manners.

response.speaker: Ono
response.text: Since Mr. Saimon trusts you, I should, too.

response.speaker: Ono
response.text: So, what can I help you with?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: About Jirou's whereabouts...

response.speaker: Ono
response.text: Ah, him... he's probably gone off to become a bandit.

response.speaker: Ono
response.text: Well, for a person of his character, being a bandit is freer than being a soldier.

response.speaker: Ono
response.text: By the way, don't tell Mr. Saimon this, or he'll get mad.

response.speaker: Ono
response.text: Jirou actually managed to convinced that scaredy-cat Ishikawa to desert together with him. He made it alright... But Ishikawa ending up eating detention barracks rations for quite a few days!

response.speaker: Ono
response.text: But even that was because Lord Masahito was kind enough to cover this up and not report it to his accursed old man. If not for that...

response.speaker: Ono
response.text: *sigh* Let's not even go there... Jirou really got Ishikawa into hot water, I'll tell you what...

response.speaker: Ono
response.text: If it wasn't for Mr. Saimon, I'd smack him silly the next time we meet!

response.speaker: Ono
response.text: Well, that's all I know about Jirou. Well, you're going to have to exercise some creativity to make that news a little less unpleasant for Mr. Saimon...

response.speaker: Ono
response.text: Ah, right. If you'd like to know more, you can go ask Ogura. He's over there by the tower, and was on duty the day it happened. He probably saw more than I did, at any rate.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thank you.

response.speaker: Ono
response.text: It was nothing, don't sweat it.

response.speaker: Ono
response.text: Also, could you not tell Lord Masahito about this?

response.speaker: Ono
response.text: Jirou was annoying, sure, but this is a matter of life and death. We're not going to go there.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Yuu
dialogues.text: You're... an outlander?

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Yuu
dialogues.text: May I ask... what you're doing here in the camp?

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Yuu
dialogues.text: If you're not on important business, please leave. This is a key military site. Unrelated persons are not permitted to enter.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm here at Saimon Katsumi's behest.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Yuu
dialogues.text: Saimon...? Ah! You mean Saimon Jirou's father!

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Yuu
dialogues.text: Sorry for my rudeness, I didn't know that you were here on the old man's request.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Yuu
dialogues.text: I'm not very familiar with Saimon Jirou, but since his family is so worried, I'll do all I can.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Jirou's whereabouts...

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Yuu
dialogues.text: That night, I saw him and Ishikawa fleeing northwards. So I followed the usual our private protocol and sounded the alarm after 15 seconds.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Yuu
dialogues.text: Usually, these few seconds would let you find a good spot to hide if you're lucky.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Yuu
dialogues.text: But we never expected that Ishikawa would trip, flip, and fall out of fright... Well, we caught him on the spot.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw...

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Yuu
dialogues.text: *sigh* That Ishikawa. I mean, you'd think that he would at least act the part of a samurai scion...

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Yuu
dialogues.text: If I don't miss my guess, Saimon Jirou has probably fled to Jinren Island, the northernmost section of Narukami Island.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Yuu
dialogues.text: Bandits who refuse to submit to the Shogunate have gathered there, and have increased in number due to the war.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Yuu
dialogues.text: Now that our attention has been shifted to the Sangonomiya and away from them, they're getting all kinds of uppity ideas.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Yuu
dialogues.text: The latest rumors even say that they've tried to set up their own independent nation, or declare a grand revolt against our great Ogosho... or some crazy nonsense like that.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Yuu
dialogues.text: Well, we weren't very well acquainted, but I do hope that Saimon Jirou hasn't thrown in with those fellows.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks for sharing what you know.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Yuu
dialogues.text: I'm just glad that I could help. I mean, everyone has family they miss.

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Yuu
dialogues.text: Ah yes. Could you... refrain from reporting this to Lord Masahito?

dialogues.speaker: Ogura Yuu
dialogues.text: The issue with the Lord Commissioner is already giving him enough of a headache. He really doesn't need any more trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
dialogues.text: You're back. Here, have a few Lavender Melon... save them for the road, if you will.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
dialogues.text: Ah yes, as for young Jirou... Is there news of him?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Uh, we should probably avoid telling him what's going on...)

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: Ah, is that so... If he is well, it is well.

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: Thank you. You've done well.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: O—Oh, it was nothing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe...

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: This is good. Ah, my boy truly is a lucky lad. A lucky lad indeed!

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: Well then! What are you two standing there for? Pack up now, let's go!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: L—Let's go...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Go where?

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: Come now! My boy Jirou has experienced so much hardship — I shall go send him some local specialties to pamper him a little!

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: He must've gone hungry and thirsty many times on the battlefield. Indeed, he must be missing the food back home madly.

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: And of course, I'll take the opportunity to drop in on Lord Kujou and ask him to "take care" of that useless son of mine, haha!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: H—Hold on!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y—Yeah... Please calm down, good sir!

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: Ah, but I am calm. In fact, I am glad! As I shall be, to see my son again...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: B—But, your son...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The battlefield he's on is super dangerous!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right! That's right! It's super dangerous there. Swords flashing as far as the eye can see, arrows falling like rain, and... and...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Cannonballs as big as Paimon falling down and exploding across the land!

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: They couldn't be that large...

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: I see... Well...

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: Didn't you just say that he's doing well?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He is, yes...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, we do what we can to survive in war.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup... Yeah, that's right! Jirou's trying so hard on the battlefield. Paimon's sure he wouldn't want you to risk yourself for his sake, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It might be impolite to say this, but you wouldn't want to burden your son further when he's in such a tough spot already, right?

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: You have a point.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Phew...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Phew...

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: But I will still go!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!?

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: Hmph! The Saimon Clan has ever been loyal! For 2,000 years we have bled for the Ogosho and slain countless evils!

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: Besides, these old bones have lived long enough. I shall fall in battle in Her Excellency's name. My honor shall not be my own — it shall also be Jirou's!

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: Just wait here: I'm going to get my heirloom gear, my glittering sword, and then I shall go out with Jirou to meet the foe. There, we shall—

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Beat them witless?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Beat them senseless?

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: Aye, we shall beat the snot out of them!

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: Old man! What are you yelling about? I'll bet they can hear you all the way over in Sangonomiya!

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: You...! How do you know that? Have you even been there!?

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: And so what if I did? I've had it up to here with you! You know what? forget Sangonomiya, I'm going to Celestia next, and you're not coming along!

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: Fine! I've lived long enough myself! I'm about to go fight those rebel scum!

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: Jirou's finally become somebody! Not like you... It's always "this isn't normal, that won't do" with you...

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: Hah! You? Go out and fight the rebels? You can barely sit down for a game of chess with the young people without talking their ears off about archon-knows-what. You're one to talk about "being somebody"!

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: And let me remind you, you've never won a single one of those chess games!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Uh, Paimon thinks we probably step in...)

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: Oh, so you think you can raise your voice at your old lady? Why don't you just try it, eh?

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: Look at you! You can't even beat me in an argument! You get to that battlefield with cannonballs that size flying in, and we'll see how you disgrace the Saimon heirlooms and sword!

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: What do you mean, I can't beat you? I've just never... I've just never been serious!

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: And if you can't get serious fighting your old lady, do you think you'll do any better against those rebels, huh?

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: You...!

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: Just you wait, old woman! Just you wait!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, should we go check on him? It wouldn't be good if he does something rash!

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: Hah, don't you worry about him!

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: ...He's gone back to his room to flip through a dictionary.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A dictionary...?

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: He needs it to figure out how to beat me in an argument.

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: Hmph. Well, he's not talking to me for the rest of week, that's for sure.

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: But that's better than him going out to the battlefield.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that right...

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: Ah, and speaking of which, youngster from abroad...

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: You lit that fire under the old coot's rear, didn't you?

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: Haha! Who were you trying to fool?

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: And it's about that brat Jirou, isn't it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yes.

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: Well, let me guess. He's alive... But for some reason, you can't tell the old man what the situation is, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Hehe...

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: *sigh* Youngster, lying is bad behavior.

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: ...That said, I'm in no position to say that you did the wrong thing.

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: Hehe, and I must say that it was thanks to your lie that I got to see that old fossil get more fired up than I've ever seen him.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We're very sorry...

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: Alright, there's no need to be polite. As it happens, I have a favor of my own to ask regarding that lad Jirou.

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: Go help me check on that child. Help us see if he's done something wrong or steered himself onto the wrong path.

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: If he has, help us teach him a little lesson.

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: Jirou's always been a smart kid, but he's always been a little too pleased with his smarts, and it sometimes blinds him.

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: I have no fear for him on the battlefield. He's always been good at surviving, no matter where he is.

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: If he really did meet an unfortunate end... Well, I've long prepared myself for this. That is the nature of war, after all.

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: I just... fear that he may get too full of himself, bite off more than he can chew, and wind up in a more dangerous position than he expects.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's how it is... We'll help you out!

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: Alright. I won't hold you two here any longer...

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: While you search for Jirou, I will help to hold the fort here with that old fool. Undo a bit of the damage you did, you know?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You have our thanks.

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: Ah, it should be me thanking you. I suspect that our tom-fool son has brought you enough trouble already.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're too kind.

choices.text: We barely made it back here ourselves.
He's just not at liberty to write to you.

dialogues.speaker: Ishikawa
dialogues.text: Outlander, what are you doing in the camp? This is a key military location.

dialogues.speaker: Ishikawa
dialogues.text: ...Well, whatever. It's not as if we haven't seen any outlanders recently or anything.

dialogues.speaker: Ishikawa
dialogues.text: If you're one of them "advisors" from Narukami Island, look for Lord Masahito directly. He'll welcome you, I'm sure.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Saimon Katsumi asked us to come here.

dialogues.speaker: Ishikawa
dialogues.text: Sorry, I don't know a Sai— wait, you mean Saimon Katsumi?

dialogues.speaker: Ishikawa
dialogues.text: Old Man Saimon from Konda Village? That's who you're talking about, right?

dialogues.speaker: Ishikawa
dialogues.text: Ah, so you're a friend of... I see. My apologies, I was rude. Is the old man still well? I hope he's still spry.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He's very worried about Jirou, his son.

dialogues.speaker: Ishikawa
dialogues.text: Ah. Um, I see.

dialogues.speaker: Ishikawa
dialogues.text: Well, we're quite worried about him too, to be honest...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What happened to him?

dialogues.speaker: Ishikawa
dialogues.text: Mm... Please don't tell the old man... And definitely don't tell Lord Masahito...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: My lips are sealed.

dialogues.speaker: Ishikawa
dialogues.text: (He left the army...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Ishikawa
dialogues.text: I mean, he deserted.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Eh!?

dialogues.speaker: Ishikawa
dialogues.text: (Quiet, you!)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, what's so special about deserting anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Ishikawa
dialogues.text: (You too!)

dialogues.speaker: Ishikawa
dialogues.text: *sigh* This war is too much to bear.

dialogues.speaker: Ishikawa
dialogues.text: We've fought quite a few battles against the rebels recently, and we've lost a lot of comrades. They were all our mutual friends...

dialogues.speaker: Ishikawa
dialogues.text: Of course, Lord Masahito tried to help us settle our emotions a little, and has assigned us garrison duties as a result.

dialogues.speaker: Ishikawa
dialogues.text: But the Lord Commissioner has been ordering him to send troops out, which must be frustrating him...

dialogues.speaker: Ishikawa
dialogues.text: Never mind. Back to Jirou, then... That fellow's always liked those stories about great bandits... "Konda Ikki" or something, that was his favorite.

dialogues.speaker: Ishikawa
dialogues.text: When you add that up with his being tired of fighting this war... I think it's possible that he might have upped and left to join the nearby bandits...

dialogues.speaker: Ishikawa
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, but that's all I know. If you want to know, you can go ask Ono. He should know more.

dialogues.speaker: Ishikawa
dialogues.text: See that guy sitting over there, sighing and hanging his head? That's Ono, you can't miss him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you very much.

dialogues.speaker: Ishikawa
dialogues.text: You're too kind. Say hi to Old Man Saimon for me, would you?
Phew, finally, someone's here to rescue me!
Thank you, thank you so much!
But we can't stay in this place. Let's split up and get out of here!
Ah, right. I know of a safe spot. Let me just mark it out for you over... here.
Just look for me there, got it? Okay. Great. Bye!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, wait a—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, he's gone off on his own. So rude!

choices.text: Well, we are a bit too close to the open sea.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's true. Let's get out of here first, then!

choices.text: The bandits will spot us any moment now.

dialogues.text: If you hadn't gotten me out of that cage, those fellows would have turned me into a blood urchin...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's a blood urchin?
Hahaha. Oh right, the two of you are outlanders. You wouldn't know our local parlance.
It's a very scary, ancient method of punishment. A very, very scary one...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Very, very, very scary...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, alright, Paimon doesn't wanna hear it! Ugh, why did Paimon even ask!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #No, wait. Actually, how did you know all this weird stuff, huh, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hehe. Why don't you try to guess?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey—!
Hahaha, alright, alright. Don't argue.
#Ah, so {NICKNAME}'s your name. Pleased to meet your acquaintance.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The pleasure is all mine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We want to ask you about a couple of things.
Ask away.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So we're looking for a certain Saimon Jirou...
Oh... him...
Why'd you want to know where he is?

response.text: I—It's nothing! I'm just asking.
I... I've heard on the grapevine that the Tenryou Commissioner's sent out lots of ninjas to capture deserters in secret.
Looking at you ask about this and that, I was starting to wonder if the things I heard were true.

choices.text: I know that I'm a ninja?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (This guy's story is just full of holes...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Let's just play along and see if we can make those holes any bigger!)
Ugh...!
I— Well, I was just saying that, you know? But yeah, what a coincidence, am I right? Haha... Ha...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Paimon, you're up.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A coincidence, you say...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, did you think that our saving you was a coincidence, then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's a fine reward out for providing information on deserters. And if none can be provided, it's no loss as long as we can catch one.
What do you mean "no loss"?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "No loss" to us, of course.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, you've got a good head on your shoulders, don't you? Shame about that...
Wh—What do you mean...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Actually, where'd you learn that line, Paimon?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Hehe! From all the people we've met on this journey, of course!)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Alright, {NICKNAME}. We've wasted enough words on him. Time to execute this deserter.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Kneel!
W—W—Wait!
My life is unimportant but before I die can I please ask to please look at your identification papers please lords can I just know your names please!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What in the world is he talking about?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: He wants to see our papers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hah! What nonsense.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A man who fled the army, trying to beg for the name of loyal samurai?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Indeed. Preposterous!
Please don't kill me I'll tell you were the treasure is just don't kill me Ogosho's tears please just don't kill meeee!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (This guy's scared out of his wits...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Come again?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Calm down. One sentence at a time.
You're... not going to kill me anymore?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But before that, we'd like to ask you another question...
Please ask.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are you Saimon Jirou?
I... maybe...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: I—I—I am! I am! I'm Jirou, alright?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, look at him grovel...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (That's true, his identity is difficult for us to ascertain. But if we send him to his parents, they'll know in a heartbeat.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, Saimon. On account of your coming from a samurai line, we'll give you one chance to redeem your errors.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now, tell us again, what... treasure were you talking about earlier? Speak clearly!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Indeed. Speak clearly!

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Well, I—I'm a professional treasure hunter...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is he?

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: S—Sorry! I'll get to the point.

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: After some lengthy investigation, I've discovered the location of some treasure nearby.

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: It's just that the treasury gate requires four stone slates to open.

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: If you could, my lords, please help me find these stone slates, that I might investigate them—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you taking us for fools?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Paimon, don't press him too hard, now.)

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: I—I wouldn't dare... I just mean that I've investigated it for a while, and have a good deal of experience.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, if you do, then you'll know better than to try to play us false.

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Once all the stone slates are in place, the treasury door should open. Then we can split the treasure... uh, thirty-seventy...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Want to die, do you?

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: You'll get seventy, I'll get thirty!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Relax, relax. This is just business. And we're definitely amenable to price negotiations.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Once we've settled on something that we can agree on, everyone will be happy, right?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Only thirty-seventy?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: True, that seems somewhat unacceptable. How about twenty-eighty?

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: That's great! Twenty-eighty it is!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Sounds good, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's send twenty percent of his fingers to the Tenryou Commissioner. We'll split the remaining eighty.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Agreed.

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Eh!? W—Wait, no! Stop! I thought...!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hands out!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Halt!

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Ah, as I thought, we can still discuss things, right...!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's no need to dirty your blade. Paimon's will do!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's smaller, so this'll go slower.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Oh, yes. True, true.

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: S—Stop! Please stop torturing me!

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: I'll give you everything. Everything, alright?

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Just take all of it... *sobs*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Wow, we made him cry...)

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: I'm quite big now... but no one has bullied me like this before... Waaah...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (We played the part a little too well, huh...?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Weakling.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Hey! Aren't we done here already!?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (We should leave.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Okay. Let's go.)

choices.text: I said nothing about looking for deserters.

dialogues.text: I mean, the key's right there! What's stopping you from getting it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, stay in that cage a moment, will you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Young lad, the world outside your cage has changed greatly since you last saw it...
What...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We must continue to observe you. We must see if you have the qualities necessary to save this world.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is a "trial."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The "trial"... of perseverance!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, Paimon recognizes you! Lord, this is the very person you saw in your dreams!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Keep silent for dramatic effect.)
Ugh, are you both done yet? Help me get that key already!

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: My lords! Here, sit, please! Sorry for the trouble...

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: ...But how goes your search for those stone slates?

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: I don't mean to pry!

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Ah, so you must have been successful, then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Please, my lords, continue speaking...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is all of them, right?

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Uh...

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Actually... No...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Say that again?

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: There's one missing.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What did you say?

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: There's one stone slate missing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What do you mean "one missing"! We worked really hard to find these four!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And now you say that we're missing one—!

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: I'm sorry, I'm sorry! I won't do that again!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I think we deserve an explanation.

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: I've actually hidden the last stone slate somewhere safe. I just wanted to guard against—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Us?

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Y—Yes...

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Uh, I mean no! Of course not!

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: I just wanted to prevent people from finding the slates ahead of me...

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: That way, the one slate that I hid away would serve as a final piece of insurance.

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Even if I couldn't obtain the other four slates, no one would be able to open the treasury.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Seems reasonable.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, where did you put that last slate?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Take us there.

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: I won't!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What?

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: I don't want to, so I won't!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Afraid of something?

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Wh—What would I be afraid of?

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: If you made me lead you there and get you the stone slate...

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: That place is where... people dispose of bodies...

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: You'd just get rid of me, wouldn't you? Wh—Why wouldn't I be scared...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, such clear logic!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, he's got a point. Why didn't we think of that?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's do it your way, then.

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Hey! I haven't told you where the stone slate is hidden yet!

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Are you just going to get rid of me... right here? The secret of the stone slate will die with me, you know?

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: J—Just spare my life, and I'll tell you where it is. And after that... I'll do whatever you tell me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Let's not press him too hard. And since he's already said this much...)

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: There's a place, beside a small waterfall, hidden amongst the cliffs across the sea from Ritou. That's where I buried the stone slate.

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: If you fear you might forget, my lords, I'll mark the location on your map later...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thanks!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: *cough*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph. Looks like you've got your uses, huh?

choices.text: Tell me where to find the slate.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: How are things going? I can already smell the treasure, haha!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm, us too!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, here they are.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: One, two, three, four... Hmm, no, that's not right.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh—?

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: We're missing one slate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This guy is untrustworthy. He's trying to play us!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's going on, Jirou?

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: D—Don't be so hasty! Let me explain.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: I hid one other stone slate beforehand — here, beside a waterfall amidst the cliffs on Ritou's opposing shore. Here, I'll mark it out on your map.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: I just need you two to go on one last trip.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really...? Paimon still thinks this is suspicious.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No tricks.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: There won't be, don't worry.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: See, if I didn't have that last slate, I wouldn't be able to get to the treasure either, would I?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then why didn't you tell us from the start?

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Well, I didn't trust you all as much then. But since you've both helped me so much, there's no reason for me to hide anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...You do have a point.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: I'll leave it to you two, then. I'll be resting here. Just look for me again once you've found it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph. Aren't you a pair of idle hands.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're doing all the work here... Maybe we should renegotiate our terms!

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Wait! We had an agreement on that one! You'll have a majority share!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you sure?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He's panicked, that's what's for sure.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, since you look like you want that treasure so desperately, we'll trust you just this once.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're definitely gonna renegotiate once we get our hands on that last stone slate.

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: Who are you? Name yourselves!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's our line. Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: What's that got to do with you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I will not cut down a nameless person.

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: Hah! You outlanders have such a rule as well?

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: How interesting...

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: There's no need to waste time here, just fight him already!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Silence, you.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Uh, okay...

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: You've come to save this kid?

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: #No, {F#she}{M#he} hasn't...

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: Silence, you!

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: A—Alright, you speak first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're here to settle a score with him!

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: Oh? What a coincidence!

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: I'm here to do just that myself!

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: In which case, I'm afraid you're going to have to get in line.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm. Would you like to know...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Who saved him the previous time?

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: You did.

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: He told me so at least a few times.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oh, then that's alright.

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: He bluffed you into helping him find the stone slate, didn't he? Bet he didn't tell you that the treasure still needs a key to open it, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A key?

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: Hah! You see, the treasury doesn't just have one gate, but three.

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: Want to open that door? Slates, key, you'll need 'em both.

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: This fellow is a little snake. Had us all fooled.

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: How about this? I suggest that you and I settle this whole treasure business between us.

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: From the looks of you, you aren't with the Shogunate. That suits me just fine. I'd sooner trust an outlander than one of those lackeys.

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: And if you can prove your ability, I'll let you into my group. It's a good deal for you!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What about Jirou?

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: Oh, him? I'll have the dogs tear him to shreds. We'll pack the pieces up and chuck 'em into the sea.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: You have other dogs?

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: What do you mean by that?

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: I mean that Toratarou doesn't bite.

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: And how do you know that?

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: He's a good dog, he wouldn't bite anyone!

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: I think you're in need of a few dog bites, alright!

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: But that's the thing. Toratarou wouldn't bite anyone! He's a real friendly dog!

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: Shut up!

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: But, but, but! Just shut up already, or do you need me to smash you, cage and everything!?

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: Now, where were we?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You were talking about a key...

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: It's on his person.

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: That smart aleck thought that he could hide the treasury key and keep all the treasure for himself.

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: But he was way too hasty for his own good. He's just full of openings!

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: Now in our line of work, the most important thing is a sense of "fairness."

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: Things don't end well for those who try to hoard everything for themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: It's just the principle of the matter, you know? And when someone doesn't listen to his brothers, then slightly... harder measures are required.

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: So he fled into the cage, locked himself inside, and threw the key away—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What...?

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: I know, right? He stunned us right into silence too.

dialogues.speaker: Bandit Leader
dialogues.text: And then he gave a cry of shock—

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: I threw the wrong key... I threw the cage key into the trees opposite us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pfft!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Bwahahahahaha! What in the world is that?

response.speaker: Bandit Leader
response.text: So, the person you're trying to save is this hapless, worthless man.

response.speaker: Bandit Leader
response.text: Not much to his character either: he's a deserter, hated by all!

response.speaker: Bandit Leader
response.text: And finally, he even got on the bad side of someone he couldn't afford to offend!

response.speaker: Bandit Leader
response.text: But you on the other hand — you're a smart person. You've got brains, brawn, and you've got your ways.

response.speaker: Bandit Leader
response.text: Between him and I, it should be pretty obvious who you should choose, eh?

choices.text: I wouldn't call myself that intelligent.

response.speaker: Bandit Leader
response.text: ...And what do you mean by that?

choices.text: The treasure. I'm taking all of it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright!

response.speaker: Bandit Leader
response.text: Is that so... Well, that's a shame. A real shame.

choices.text: I'll take both him and the treasure.
I'd say you're the unintelligent one here.

talks.objective: Find Saimon Jirou on Jinren Island

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: N—No! D—Don't come any closer!

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Noooo! I wanna go home! I don't wanna be a bandit! Or a treasure hunter!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Calm down, Jirou.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There, there... We're here to rescue. We're gonna take you home.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: No! No! I want to live! I still want to see my mother...!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Agh, now Paimon's feeling guilty...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Just look at him! Paimon doesn't think he's gonna listen to a word you say... We might as well just keep up the act!)

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Stop! Stop! Don't come any closer!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hey, listen here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: I—It's like this, alright?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You've caused us lots of trouble, and your repeated deceptions are a sin that cannot be atoned for!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: However!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You have contributed to the Shogun's righteous cause in aiding in the defeat of these bandits!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: By these actions have you thus redeemed yourself, and thus, you shall not be punished. Indeed, we shall bring you home to be reunited with your parents!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Indeed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, Jirou, are you alright?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hello! Jirou! Are you there?

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Is this...

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Is this... some kind of newfangled interrogation technique?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Pfft! No, it isn't! We're going to bring you home! C'mon, aren't you happy?

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Oh...

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Ohh...

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Ohhhh!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, what are you trying to do, bite someone?

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: ...So you're saying that not only am I not going to be "dealt with," but that I made a contribution, right?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Th—That is the case, yes.

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Hahaha! That's right, that's right! That was my intention all along!

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: I won't beleaguer you with the details, but I was merely baiting those crooks in when I was captured the previous two times...

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: I redirected you and intentionally got myself captured, for I had calculated perfectly that you would find me here, just as I fell into the trap!

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: But little did they know that I had risked myself to serve as the lure while you closed the net! Ah, like the praying mantis hunting the cicada, they did not see th—

choices.text: We were just randomly passing by.

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: *sigh* Indeed, even the wisest of the wise cannot account for every coincidence.

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Of course, I'm not calling myself wise here. I am a very humble person, after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, and here we were worried that we might have scared the stupid out of him...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seems like this guy has forgotten everything.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'd say that his thick skin is a small miracle in and of itself.

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Hehe. Well, now that you've said all this, I feel like there's no need to go home just yet!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* This guy is... Ugh, he's such a waste of our breath!

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Why don't we just get all that treasure while we're at it. Two big scores in one day shall set us all at ease.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph. *If* there's any treasure, you mean...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But why don't we go have a look anyway? We've come all this way. It'd be a shame not to take some of that treasure~

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: That's more like it! Here's the key. Don't lose it, now.

choices.text: You know what, I'm actually quite glad.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey—!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What in the world is all this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *cough* Pah...! So much ash!

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: We've looked all over the place. Nothing but rotten provisions and old pottery...

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Famous swords and armor, precious gems and gold... There's nothing like that here.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: There's nothing hidden underneath, either...

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Why did this happen?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! You aren't tricking us again, are you!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh...? But there's nothing here!

choices.text: I think I get what happened...

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: What is this!? We did so much, planned for so long, but in the end...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, come on, don't get too down...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's go home, Jirou.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, come on, there's no need to be so sad. Let's go home, shall we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe you think that returning home empty-handed might be embarrassing, but actually, it's fine...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You've been through three super dangerous adventures, and you survived.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The mistakes you've made have also been made up for. Though you didn't get the treasure you expected, you didn't lose anything in the end anyway...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Compared to all those dangers you've been through, being scolded by your dad is nothing, right?

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Alright...

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Let's go home, Jirou.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Yay! We did it!)

choices.text: I'll explain it to you later, Paimon.
He isn't tricking us this time.

talks.objective: Open the "treasury" front door using the key

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
dialogues.text: Haha! My Jirou's back!

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
dialogues.text: You little brat! Bet you've been slacking off instead of fighting for Her Excellency like you ought to have, eh? And to top it off, you didn't even have time to write to me!

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: Working hard at everything but fighting, am I right?

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: Wait. What do you mean?

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: It means you're an old mouth breather...

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: This kid can always count on your falling for his fibs. But not me — I always see through his little lies.

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: I'll bet he ran away to have his own little adventures because he thought army life was hard, boring, and dangerous.

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: ...Just like you when you were young.

response.speaker: Saimon Eri
response.text: Lazy, impatient, and feckless, but fond of a good brag. Ah, you men are all the same...

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: Hey! Why'd you start trashing me all of a sudden?

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi
response.text: Let him speak for himself! What happened?

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Katsumi

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Katsumi

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Katsumi

dialogues.text: "It has been over a year since my son, Saimon Jirou, joined the army. He would write letters to us from time to time, and though he has not accomplished much of great note, he would relate everything that happened to him in the army, which comforted this old man's heart greatly."

dialogues.speaker: Missing Person Bulletin Board
dialogues.text: "The war has continued apace, and my son, who has accomplished little, has stopped sending any letters. This lack of contact has greatly disturbed and wounded this old man's spirit."

dialogues.speaker: Missing Person Bulletin Board
dialogues.text: "I beseech any who see the notice to help me search for my son. If you know of his whereabouts, whether he ekes out some existence somewhere or has had the fortune of dying for his nation, please let me know, that I may have peace in my heart."

dialogues.speaker: Missing Person Bulletin Board
dialogues.text: "If you have anything to discuss, I, Saimon Katsumi give you my sincere thanks."

response.speaker: Saimon Katsumi

dialogues.text: By which he means that he deserted.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh!

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Come on, "deserting" is such a bad word. I prefer something like...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Absconding?"

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: What on earth is that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What on earth is that?

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Right, I remember now. This is what we call "transferring investments!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: He means going off to become a bandit.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah!

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: How did you know that I—

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I just guessed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Haha, he gave himself up!

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Hmph...

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Alright, alright. Let's not talk about this stuff... We'll have all the time in the world to talk nonsense once the stone slates have all been found.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Alright.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Well, you continue then. If you'd like to rest for a while over here, that's fine too.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Ah, my lords! You've returned.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: How is it? How goes your search.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Be quiet, whelp.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (How are you this experienced...)

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Y—Yes, I'm sorry! I spoke out of turn, out of turn!

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Please, my lords, rest your weary feet here, and continue on your way once you are rested as you please...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mm.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mm~

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Oh, you're back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you've been quite idle here, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Haha, there's no need to put it like that.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Sit as you please and have something to eat. This tent of mine isn't too bad, I hope!

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Ah, yes. How goes the search for the stone slates?

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: So quickly? Ah, I should have expected no less from travelers from abroad who move as they please through Inazuma!

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: No need to rush. At this rate, the day I get rich is not far off, I'd wager!

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Uh... *cough*, I mean, "we."

response.speaker: Saimon Jirou
response.text: Aye, what say we all get rich together, eh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph. What a fishy guy...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, he's really ignoring us...

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: I'm Saimon Jirou! I'm Saimon Jirou, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: The treasure's all yours! I won't take a single Mora!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Let's not get him too much more worked up than this. He's such a wretched guy...)

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: If you hadn't gotten me out of that cage, those fellows would have turned me into a blood urchin...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's a blood urchin?

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Hahaha. Oh right, the two of you are outlanders. You wouldn't know our local parlance.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: It's a very scary, ancient method of punishment. A very, very scary one...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Very, very, very scary...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, alright, Paimon doesn't wanna hear it! Ugh, why did Paimon even ask!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #No, wait. Actually, how did you know all this weird stuff, huh, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hehe. Why don't you try to guess?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey—!

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Hahaha, alright.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: #So you're called {NICKNAME}. My name is Saimon Jirou. Pleased to meet you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The pleasure is all mine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm. That's right, we still don't know how you ended up in that cage.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Well, this is a bit embarrassing... But I was just trying to get some peace of mind from my naggy old father...

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Never thought I'd wander right into a nest of bandits and get myself kidnapped!

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: If not for you, I'd be in mortal danger for sure!

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Ah, yes, I forget. I should probably give you some reward for this deed. My apologies.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, you're too polite...

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: So, as for the reward...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, yep?

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, but I can't give it to you right now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Come on, then why did you leave us hanging like that?

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Whoa, no need to rush. Just slow down a bit and let me talk.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Well, I—I'm a professional treasure hunter.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Professional treasure hunter? Never heard of that...

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Uh, I mean, I'm someone who looks for treasure for a living.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, Paimon's got it now!

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: After some lengthy investigation, I've discovered the location of some treasure nearby.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: It's just that the treasury gate requires four stone slates to open.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you want us to run your errands for you?

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: C'mon, don't be so hard up! If you bring the stone slates to me, and let me open the treasury door for you, I won't take a single Mora. The treasure will all be yours.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's so fishy...

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: I mean, you did save my life! What's some treasure compared to that?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can't be sure if we can trust you...

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Hehe, ah, see I knew you'd be too kind to take it all.

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: How about this, then? We'll split it thirty-seventy. Seventy for me, twenty for you, and we'll give that last ten to the Ogosho in taxes. How about that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Why do we have to split the loot with the Shogun?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're not making any sense...

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: It's a huge treasury, you know? Even twenty percent is a sizable amount!

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: And it's better than getting nothing, am I right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Didn't you say that you weren't going to take a single Mora?

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Hehe, that was a limited-time offer — you snooze, you lose!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This guy—!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We'll settle this score once we find that treasure, mark Paimon's words!

dialogues.speaker: Saimon Jirou
dialogues.text: Please go, you two. Time waits for no one!
